sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Republic of Panama) / Private Interest Foundation (PIF) vehicle
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA), entered into force 31 October 2012
Panama–European Union Association Agreement, provisionally applicable since 2013
Panama–United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement, in force 2021
Panama–Republic of Korea Double Taxation Convention

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 30 April 2015 (amended by Law 70 of 2019) establishing the AML/CFT framework; Executive Decree No. 1 of 20 October 2022 creating the Registry of Ultimate Beneficial Owners; Resolution No. 1 of 2015 of the Financial Analysis Unit (Unidad de Análisis Financiero – UAF); Private Interest Foundation Law (Law 25 of 12 June 1995).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the founder's valid passport or national identity card, apostilled or legalized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent issuing authority of the founder's country (e.g., national registry, foreign ministry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the country is not a party to the 1961 Hague Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or corporate existence for a corporate founder (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the jurisdiction where the corporate founder is formed

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Panamanian registered agent and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the founder's country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the founder, foundation council members, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Panamanian national restrictive list, Interpol Red Notices, and FATF high-risk jurisdiction register; enhanced customer due diligence (CDD) for politically exposed persons (PEPs) and for beneficial owners domiciled in high-risk jurisdictions; all documentary evidence must be preserved for at least five years in accordance with Law 23 of 2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama) – Online Name Reservation and Filing System (website: https://www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation name must employ Latin script. If the commercial name is in a non-Latin language, a standard transliteration into Spanish is required for the registry index. The name must contain the designation 'Fundación', 'Foundation', or an accepted abbreviation (e.g., 'F.') to indicate private interest foundation status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If name reservation is rejected, the applicant may submit an administrative reconsideration to the Director of the Public Registry within 15 business days after the rejection notice, with a proposed substitute name. If the director sustains the rejection, the applicant may appeal to the Third Chamber of the Supreme Court of Panamá (Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo) filing a 'demanda contencioso-administrativa' within 30 calendar days. Re-applying for a different name ab initio remains possible at any time.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for satisfying the registered-address requirement, but the foundation must retain a licensed Panamanian registered agent with a physical address in Panama. The B2B SaaS scope does not mandate local personnel or a brick-and-mortar operation; substance is assessed based on the registered agent, local office address, and the administrative/management functions actually conducted in Panama.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5% (low risk – no statutory license; unannounced on-site inspections are possible by UAF/Public Registry for AML compliance, but low probability given the non-regulated nature)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and reservation at the Public Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official tariff for online name reservation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary public fee for execution of the foundation charter (Acta Constitutiva)
Registration fee for the foundation deed at the Public Registry
Filing of ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) record under Executive Decree 1 of 2022
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Público de Panamá / Ministry of Economy and Finance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of foreign founding documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent foreign authority (e.g., Secretary of State, Foreign Ministry, Notary)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional drafting of foundation charter, internal rules and opening operational resolution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat professional fee for PIF formation and AML consultation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and international sanctions screening of founder and beneficial owner
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance data provider (e.g., Dow Jones, World-Check)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market subscription fee per individual screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and registered office annual retainer (first year)
Certified Spanish translation of any foreign-language incorporation documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn Public Translator (Traductor Público Autorizado) in Panama

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley N° 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Regime), Articles 1-46, as amended by Ley N° 41 de 2014 and Decreto Ejecutivo N° 44 de 2014
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (Notarized Public Deed of Foundation Charter), inscribed under the Folio Electrónico system
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum declared patrimony of USD 10,000 per Article 18 of Law 25 of 1995; no paid-up capital or escrow deposit is required at formation — the Founder's sworn declaration of intended asset transfer is sufficient
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the endowment of not less than USD 10,000 declared by the Founder is hereby acknowledged and irrevocably dedicated to the Foundation's purposes, and the Foundation Council accepts its stewardship.

RESOLVED, that the registered office located at the address specified in the Foundation Charter is adopted as the statutory seat, and the Resident Agent licensed under Law 25 of 1995 is confirmed.

RESOLVED, that the following officers are appointed: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, who are authorized to open bank accounts, execute commercial contracts, engage SaaS service providers and payment processors, and administer Foundation assets according to the internal bylaws for the exclusive benefit of the beneficiaries.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de Circuito, Panama City, Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Panamanian licensed attorney (abogado idóneo) to draft the Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación) including founder identification, foundation name, registered office, purposes, initial patrimony declaration, founder reserved powers, Foundation Council appointment rules, and the Resident Agent designation. Execute the deed before a Notary for inclusion in the notarial protocol.
required_dossiers: Resident Agent acceptance certificate from a licensed attorney or fiduciary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial review queries are cured by drafting the corrective clause and re-notarizing an amendment before the same Notary prior to registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry Inscription at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first testimonio (certified copy) of the notarized Foundation Charter together with the registry cover sheet; pay the inscription tariff calculated on the charter page count; the Section assigns a Folio Electrónico and issues the registration entry after legal review.
required_dossiers: First testimonio of the notarized Foundation Charter
Resident Agent consent annotated in the charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registry officials issue a defect note (nota) granting 5 business days to cure the observed defect; a corrective deed is notarized and re-submitted; if the term lapses, a new filing is made with a formal appeal to the Registrador General.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Certificaciones Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the Certificado de Personería Jurídica and an authenticated copy of the registered charter once inscription is final; the certificate serves as conclusive proof of the Foundation's legal personality and is required for all subsequent commercial and banking steps.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains discrepancies, file a written rectification request with the Certificaciones Section and obtain a corrected certificate without a charter amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RUC Registration with the Tax Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, via the T@S portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Foundation's RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) in the SISTEMA T@S under the territorial-income regime; obtain the digital FIEL electronic signature; comply with annual sworn return obligations (Información Anual del Contribuyente); the Foundation remains exempt from Panamanian income tax on foreign-source enterprise software revenue.
required_dossiers: Resident Agent identification and power of attorney
Registered office lease or ownership title
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: DGI holds are cured by uploading the requested supporting document through T@S within the statutory term; a written response to the nota de requerimiento is submitted, with escalation through the DGI Mesa de Ayuda if no resolution is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía de Panamá — Dirección de Rentas Municipales
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación for the Foundation's administrative office under the municipal economic activities classifier for information services; pay the annual patente municipal tariff and obtain the municipal operating certificate for the registered office.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or ownership title of the registered office
Fire safety certificate for the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal reviewers may request recategorization of the CAU economic code; submit a corrective sworn declaration and pay any tariff difference, with an administrative appeal available before the Municipal Director of Revenue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foundation Council Organization and Statutory Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal governance — Foundation Council under the Foundation Charter and internal regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the Foundation Council, pass the First Board Resolution, adopt the internal regulations (reglamento interno), appoint the President, Secretary and Treasurer, and open the statutory corporate books (minutes of council resolutions, registry of beneficiaries, and financial records); these books remain at the registered office and are not filed for public registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectification of internal records is effected by a subsequent Foundation Council resolution; identity discrepancies are cured by a notarized amended acceptance deed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — administrative reference only; no sectoral industrial permit applies to ISIC 6201 enterprise software activities, which are limited to municipal registration
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación de Empresa and Patente Municipal (Municipal Business Operation Notice and Annual Patent)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Categoría Exenta): pure office-based information technology services produce no physical transformation or industrial effluents, so no Category I or II EIA report or environmental registration is required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharges or VOC emissions generated. Applicable compliance limits: proper e-waste disposal under Panama's RAEE regulations (Decreto Ejecutivo N° 1 de 2016); domestic-sanitary wastewater must meet municipal sewer ordinances and general water-discharge standards under Decreto Ejecutivo N° 26 de 2018; hazardous waste only from standard office IT equipment maintenance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (Certificado de Seguridad contra Incendios) for the registered office; structural and occupancy inspection by the Municipality of Panama; workplace ergonomic and electrical safety compliance under CONASSOS (Consejo Nacional de Seguridad y Salud Ocupacional) standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI) - General Directorate of Revenue, Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), Panama; online tax portal: SITIO (Sistema Integrado de Tributacion en Linea) at https://sitio.dgi.gob.pa and national digital services portal https://www.panamadigital.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation (PIF) organized under Law 25 of 1995: (1) register the foundation charter with the Public Registry (Registro Publico) and obtain the certificate of incorporation; (2) maintain the mandatory resident agent (agente residente); (3) if conducting commercial activities generating Panamanian-source income, obtain an RUC (Registro Unico de Contribuyente) from DGI by filing Form DGI-UR-01 via SITIO with notarized and apostilled constitutive documents, proof of resident agent, and officer identification; (4) if the PIF exclusively owns foreign assets and derives foreign-source SaaS income, no RUC/ITBMS registration is mandatory, but voluntary registration is recommended to claim ITBMS export zero-rating and refunds; (5) issue the Aviso de Operacion for any physical nexus; (6) obtain a DGI-accredited digital signature certificate (Firma Electronica) to authenticate electronic filings and e-invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama applies territorial (source-based) taxation: non-resident PIFs and resident PIFs are taxable only on Panamanian-source income (Codigo Fiscal Art. 694). Under Law 25 of 1995, a PIF may elect a purely private non-commercial status with no income-tax filing duty, or elect to engage in commercial activities, becoming entity-level taxed only on Panamanian-source profits. No US-style check-the-box election exists; however, Law 254 of 2021 (fiscal modernization) incorporates BEPS hybrid-mismatch rules that may recharacterize a PIF treated as transparent in another jurisdiction. For ITBMS, a PIF with annual sales under USD 36,000 may elect the simplified small-taxpayer regime (regimen simplificado de pequenos contribuyentes).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS - Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (VAT-equivalent, Codigo Fiscal Title IV, Arts. 1057 et seq.)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Standard regime: no monetary threshold - registration is mandatory for any person habitually supplying taxable goods or services in Panamanian territory. Simplified small-taxpayer regime (Pevmes): optional for annual taxable turnover up to USD 36,000; mandatory registration applies upon crossing any taxable transaction that generates Panamanian-source revenue.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing (facturacion electronica) for all ITBMS-registered taxpayers: invoices must be issued through the DGI SITIO e-invoicing platform or an authorized private billing provider. Each invoice is validated by DGI with a unique digital acceptance code (Codigo de Aceptacion) and QR verification; real-time clearance uses REST/SOAP API integration and an X.509 digital signature from a DGI-accredited certification authority. Taxpayers must transmit invoice data to DGI in nearly real time (daily), submit monthly XML aggregates, and retain electronic records for 7 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS 0% applies to: (i) exports of goods evidenced by a customs export declaration; and (ii) services supplied from Panama to non-resident clients whose benefit is wholly realized abroad and whose consideration is paid from outside Panama (Codigo Fiscal Art. 1059-B; DGI interpretative resolutions). B2B Enterprise SaaS qualifies when the counterparty is a foreign enterprise, the software is delivered via cloud and used exclusively outside Panama, no Panamanian-domiciled user or benefit arises, and payment is remitted from foreign bank accounts or payment rails (e.g., Stripe, Wise, SWIFT). Services benefiting a Panamanian customer or used within Panama remain taxable at 7%. Taxpayers must hold exporter service status registered in the DGI export module to issue zero-rated invoices; monthly ITBMS returns must disclose zero-rated export transactions to generate refundable credit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Declaracion Unica Aduanera) for physical goods; not applicable to pure cloud SaaS
Bill of Lading (BL) or Airway Bill (AWB) for physical exports evidencing movement of goods
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103/bank statement proving receipt of payment from the non-resident customer
Signed B2B Enterprise SaaS subscription agreement identifying the Panamanian PIF as supplier and the foreign customer
Offshore service-delivery evidence: cloud datacenter location report, server/IP geolocation logs, or hosting certificate proving use outside Panama
Zero-rated electronic export invoice issued through SITIO showing the 0% ITBMS line item and DGI acceptance code
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audits export zero-rating claims within the 5-year assessment period (6 years for unregistered entities). If foreign-use or foreign-payment documentation is deficient, the 0% rate is retroactively revoked: 7% ITBMS is assessed on the full invoice amount, monthly interest of 1% applies under the Codigo Fiscal, and fines range from 50% of the omitted tax (serious infraction) to 200% (fraud), with refund clawback plus interest. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days, without an approved DGI extension, rebuts the offshore-payment requirement and recharacterizes revenue as Panamanian-source, triggering the same assessment, interest, and penalties. False export documentation exposes officers to criminal tax-fraud prosecution and removal from the DGI exporter registry.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no issuing central bank. The apex banking regulator is the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); the fiscal and tax administration authority is the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) through the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI); the AML/CFT financial intelligence unit is the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF). The US Dollar circulates as exclusive legal tender under Panama's dollarized monetary system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full currency convertibility exists for both current-account and capital-account transactions. The US Dollar is legal tender, the Balboa exists only as a fractional coin at 1:1 parity, and no exchange-control authorization, convertibility restriction, foreign-exchange rationing, or profit-remittance approval is required. B2B SaaS subscription invoices and foundation capital contributions can be freely transferred in and out; practical friction arises only from bank-level FATCA, CRS, and enhanced-due-diligence screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation for export or SaaS service proceeds. Receipts may remain indefinitely in any Panamanian or offshore account, be reinvested, or be disbursed abroad without central-bank or SBP consent because the domestic legal tender is the US Dollar.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Aporte de Capital) plus USD operational current account
USD operational corporate account with treasury and multi-currency overlay
USD enterprise operating account linked to global clearing rails
Foundation capital escrow and operational account under enhanced due diligence
Transactional USD account for B2B SaaS collections and vendor payments

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium with legal constraints. Panama has no dedicated e-money institution (EMI) licensing statute, and SBP-regulated deposit-taking or payment processing may not be conducted by unlicensed offshore fintechs. Wise and Stripe Billing/Treasury are legally viable only as payment-facilitation and collection rails operating through a licensed sponsor bank or correspondent clearing relationship; a Private Interest Foundation should maintain its primary treasury and escrow accounts at a Tier-1 Panamanian bank and use offshore EMIs as ancillary settlement conduits.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical or high-assurance video KYC interview is effectively mandatory: Tier-1 Panamanian banks require at least one Foundation Council member and the appointed resident agent to complete an in-person compliance interview at branch or a bank-approved video session supported by notarized and apostilled documentation. Pure remote account opening is not available to non-resident-controlled Private Interest Foundations. The submission file must include registry certificates from the Registro Público de Panamá, the apostilled foundation deed, passports, proof of address, council resolutions, and CRS/FATCA self-certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ultimate beneficial ownership: PIF segregated patrimony, discretionary beneficiaries, and Foundation Council structure obscure the natural persons exercising control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled Acto Constitutivo and Estatutos of the foundation; public-registry certificate from the Fundaciones section of the Registro Público de Panamá; certificate of incumbency naming all Council members; beneficial-owner declaration under Panama Law 23 of 2015; certified passport copies; sworn source-of-funds letter; and a Panamanian counsel opinion confirming legitimate private-patrimony purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border B2B SaaS revenue pattern: recurrent enterprise subscription inflows attributed to a low-substance Panamanian foundation with rapid onward disbursements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited IFRS financial statements; DGI income-tax (ISR) and ITBMS filings with payment receipts; signed enterprise MSAs/SLAs and recurring invoices; Foundation Council minutes approving treasury policy; a substance memorandum evidencing actual decision-making from Panama and resident-agent oversight; and a treasury audit trail linking every invoice to its SWIFT MT103 credit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, AML, or PEP flags on beneficial owners, foreign Council members, or counterparty jurisdictions in the SaaS client portfolio.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent World-Check or LexisNexis sanctions and PEP screening report dated within 90 days; completed PEP declarations; net-worth and source-of-wealth file for high-net-worth individuals; certified nil-SAR history with the Unidad de Análisis Financiero where applicable; and a legal memo documenting the commercial rationale of each restricted-jurisdiction counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank-license circumvention or structuring indicators: reliance on offshore EMI-only clearing, frequent sub-threshold credits, or pass-through layering without commercial documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written anti-structuring treasury policy; Foundation Council resolution centralizing all clearing through the Tier-1 bank; KYC package of the EMI and its licensing evidence; itemized invoice-to-wire reconciliation ledger; and a notarized undertaking confirming the foundation does not conduct unauthorized deposit-taking or third-party payment services.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions are routed by SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the investor's or beneficial owner's bank to the foundation's segregated USD account at a Tier-1 SBP-licensed bank, with beneficiary name exactly matching the registered foundation and reference 'Aporte de Capital - FIP PA_PIF'. The receiving bank verifies the apostilled foundation deed, Registro Público excerpt, Council capital-resolution and source-of-funds file before crediting; non-cash SaaS asset or enterprise-contract contributions are supported by an independent valuation and notarized Council minutes. No government-side capital authorization is required, but the bank performs CRS/FATCA entity-classification screening.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct USD vendor, professional-fee, and beneficiary-distribution payments, each carrying the commercial invoice reference; (2) ICC UCP600 commercial letters of credit issued by the Panamanian Tier-1 bank for hardware, data-center, and infrastructure procurement; and (3) the SBP-supervised local ACH for domestic USD operating payments such as payroll, rent, and legal or resident-agent fees. Stripe Billing and Wise B2B APIs serve as collection-only conduits for recurring SaaS subscription receivables, with automated reconciliation into the principal Tier-1 account; every outbound and inbound flow must reconcile to executed MSAs/SLAs and may not be split to evade internal thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla OTC FX forwards (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, CHF/USD) with SBP-licensed banks or Tier-1 international dealers to hedge B2B SaaS receivables denominated in non-USD currencies
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, USD/GBP) with investment-grade counterparties, permissible under SBP derivatives guidance and IFRS hedge-accounting requirements
Purchased plain-vanilla FX options (long calls and puts only) to hedge net foreign-currency invoice exposure without speculative short optionality
Onshore and offshore spot conversion for operational liquidity, unrestricted because the Panamanian legal tender is the US Dollar

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing limited-convertibility emerging-market currencies, legally permissible but practically executed through offshore global banks due to Panama's thin local NDF market

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Franchise Tax for Private Interest Foundation (Impuesto Anual de Franquicia / Tasa Única Anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Ingresos Públicos (ANIP), successor to the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI); remitted by the foundation's registered resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March; applies in full even when the foundation is dormant or derives no Panama-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues monthly statutory surcharge interest and fines under the Panama Tax Code; non-payment for two consecutive years exposes the foundation to administrative dissolution and strike-off from the Registro Público de Panamá, requiring judicial reinstatement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Confirmation Filing (Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Beneficiario Final online registry; submission effected through the foundation's registered resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: annual confirmation due on the foundation's registration-anniversary cycle established by the Public Registry, plus ad hoc filing within 30 days of any change in the founder, Foundation Council member, protector, or beneficiaries
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update carries monetary fines from USD 1,000 to USD 10,000 per entity and suspension of registry services for the foundation until the declaration is rectified.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit is imposed on a non-commercial Panama Private Interest Foundation. An audit obligation arises only if the foundation generates Panama-source taxable income and falls within the general income-tax regime requiring audited financial statements (generally annual gross revenue exceeding USD 2,500,000), if ANIP/DGI expressly requires one, or if the foundation presents financial statements to regulated third parties. A PIF should not itself habitually operate the active B2B SaaS business; the operating activity would normally be held through a Panamanian corporation in which the foundation owns shares.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IFRS Foundation is the accepted reporting framework; Panama Local GAAP is permitted for small taxpayers; no statutory accounting framework applies to a non-commercial foundation with exclusively foreign-source income under Panama's territorial tax system.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Private Interest Foundation issues no shares; 'shareholding transfers' therefore do not apply and are superseded by amendments to the foundation's beneficial composition, including substitution of beneficiaries and appointment or removal of Foundation Council members or a protector, pursuant to powers reserved in the Foundation Charter. The resident agent must maintain the UBO register and file the annual sworn UBO confirmation through the Registro Público de Panamá Beneficiario Final system; any beneficial-ownership change must be deposited within 30 days, and non-compliance attracts fines of USD 1,000 to USD 10,000.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Foundation Charter (Escritura de Fundación) and all registered amendment instruments
Register of Founder, Beneficiaries and Protector (if any)
Minute Book of the Foundation Council (Libro de Actas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 – USD 1,200 per annum for resident agent and registered office, UBO confirmation and franchise tax processing; exclusive of the USD 300 annual franchise tax captured in the matrix
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable for a non-commercial PIF; where a voluntary certified IFRS audit is procured for a small SaaS holding structure, typical fees range from USD 6,000 to USD 18,000 per audit cycle

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% Panamanian corporate income tax (ISR) on Panamanian-source taxable income; the first USD 50,000 of net taxable income is taxed at 15% and the excess at 25%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial tax regime: foreign-source income derived by a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is exempt from Panamanian ISR when the service is rendered and used outside Panama. Export Services Exemption under Article 708-C of the Fiscal Code: 100% ISR, dividend tax, and remittance tax exemption for qualifying B2B SaaS exporters maintaining at least 12 Panamanian-domiciled employees and deriving at least 75% of total revenue from exported services. PIF-specific status: an inactive PIF holding assets pays only the flat annual franchise tax of USD 300; a PIF actively carrying on ISIC 6201 software development is subject to standard ISR solely on Panama-source income, while its foreign-source element remains exempt.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 600 (Declaracion Jurada Anual del Impuesto sobre la Renta); filed exclusively through the Panamanian tax authority's online portal ATY Digital / e-DGI at https://aty.dgi.gob.pa.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual ISR return must be filed and paid within the first three (3) calendar months after the close of the taxable year; for calendar-year taxpayers the deadline is 31 March. No automatic extension is available; a discretionary deferment must be pre-approved by the Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panamanian-source gross income (Ingresos Brutos de Fuente Panamena): all SaaS subscription fees and software licensing revenue from clients invoiced and economically rendered in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs must declare Panama-source revenues only when the SaaS service is performed or utilized in Panama, and must exclude amounts attributable to a foreign permanent establishment or to contracts fully performed and consumed abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source gross income (Ingresos de Fuente Extranjera): revenue derived from B2B SaaS contracts with foreign clients where the service is delivered, accessed, and economically used outside Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report as exempt foreign-source income only where written contracts and evidence of server/operational delivery support a foreign source; attach the Article 708-C export-services exemption certificate where claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions (Costos y Deducciones): payroll, cloud hosting, software development tools, rent, utilities, and other ordinary expenses attributable to the production of Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers may deduct only expenses factually sustained in Panama and traceable to Panamanian-source revenue; costs allocated to a foreign permanent establishment are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments and credits (Anticipos y Creditos): monthly Form 651 ISR provisional payments and withholding tax credits suffered on Panamanian-source interest or dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit monthly advance payments and attach official payment vouchers; a PIF with no Panama-source income will carry zero advance credits and file a nil or non-taxable return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income and ISR payable (Renta Neta Imponible e ISR Causado): compute 15% on the first USD 50,000 and 25% on the excess of Panama-source net income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs not physically present in Panama continue to submit Form 600 to maintain the foundation's good-standing status, declaring exempt foreign-source income separately and paying the USD 300 annual franchise tax through the PIF module.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: surcharge of 10% of the tax due plus monthly delinquency interest of 1% on the unpaid amount, compounded; false or incomplete returns invoke Article 762 Fiscal Code fines of USD 50 to USD 10,000, and automatic revocation of the export-services tax exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 651 (Declaracion Mensual de Anticipos del Impuesto sobre la Renta); filed through the ATY Digital portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Payable and filed monthly no later than the last day of the month following the corresponding month's accrual; a final settlement is reconciled in Form 600.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Monthly net taxable income and the applicable advance rate (typically 2% of gross revenue for enterprises, or 15%/25% effective rate method).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PIF with no Panamanian-source income may claim an exemption from monthly advances by filing a declaration of absence of Panama-source revenue, subject to DGI confirmation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholdings and transferable credits (Retenciones y Creditos): tax withheld by clients on SaaS invoices, advance payments made in prior months.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs must ensure that Panamanian clients correctly withhold the 6% creditable withholding on service invoices and remit the same to DGI.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Omission or late filing: 10% late-payment surcharge plus 1% monthly interest on the unpaid advance; repeated failure to file Form 651 may result in a DGI assessment of estimated tax and disqualification of the PIF's registry license.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends or profit distributions made by a Panamanian entity out of Panama-source net profits. Dividends sourced from exempt foreign-source income are not subject to this tax; distributions made by a Private Interest Foundation to beneficiaries under the foundation's final purpose are legally characterized as asset distributions and are not dividends subject to the 10% WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A reduced withholding rate is available only under a DTA in force (e.g., Mexico, Barbados, UAE, Qatar, Spain, Portugal, Luxembourg, Chile, France; confirmation of entry into force is required). Protocol: (1) the non-resident beneficial owner obtains an official Certificate of Tax Residency (TRC) from its home tax authority; (2) the TRC, a Beneficial Ownership Declaration, and a DGI reduced-withholding application are delivered to the Panamanian withholding agent before payment; (3) the withholding agent files the application through the ATY platform and retains originals for five years; (4) relief is denied if the recipient fails the beneficial-owner test or lacks economic substance in its jurisdiction. Statutory DTA rates commonly result in 5% or 10% dividend WHT according to the instrument.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory remittance tax (Impuesto de Remesa) of 12.5% final withholding applies to Panamanian-source interest, royalties, software licensing fees, and technical service payments remitted abroad, subject to specific exemptions for qualified export financing and bank deposits (the latter typically taxed at 6%). Treaty rates generally reduce interest and royalty withholding to 5% or 10% (e.g., Mexico-Panama: interest 10%, royalties 10%; Barbados-Panama: interest 10%, royalties 10%). Royalties for the use of the PIF's software IP in Panama are always treated as Panama-source and trigger the remittance tax unless a full Article 708-C exemption is proven.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD thresholds: a Local File (detailed documentation report) is mandatory when the aggregate value of related-party transactions executed by the Panamanian entity equals or exceeds USD 3,000,000 per fiscal year; a Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated gross revenue equals or exceeds USD 50,000,000; a Country-by-Country Report applies where consolidated group revenue exceeds USD 750,000,000. A Transfer Pricing Informative Declaration must be filed with Form 600 when related-party intercompany transactions exceed USD 1,000,000 in the fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Panamanian Economic Substance Regulations (Law 70 of 2019, Executive Decree 179 of 2019) apply to a PIF that is tax-resident in Panama and derives relevant income from specified activities. A PIF engaged in B2B SaaS that licenses internally developed software IP may be classified under the Intellectual Property activity and must demonstrate: (a) board meetings held physically in Panama with substantive management decisions; (b) qualified employees and adequate premises located in Panama; and (c) core income-generating expenditure in Panama. Failure to satisfy the tests results in financial penalties, dissolution of the foundation, and loss of PIF tax neutrality; a pure equity holding PIF is exempt but must file an ESR notification and simplified annual declaration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately excluding Panamanian-source SaaS subscription revenues from Form 600; characterizing Panama-rendered services as foreign-source income; fabricating Article 708-C export-services exemption documentation; or using the PIF's registered agent address solely to shield taxable commercial revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud (defraudacion fiscal) under Articles 761-762 of the Fiscal Code: imprisonment of one (1) to five (5) years, a fine equal to 100%-200% of the evaded tax, full repayment of tax, monthly 1% delinquency interest and the 10% late-filing surcharge; retroactive revocation of all export-services tax benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers, directors, the PIF's designated secretary, and the registered agent may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax and penalties; court orders may include asset freezing, travel bans, dissolution of the foundation, and a judicial declaration prohibiting the responsible natural persons from serving as Panamanian corporate officers for up to ten (10) years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a PIF as a mere shell: no physical office or staff in Panama, no board minutes or accounting records for the SaaS business, no economic substance linked to the software IP contracts, or using the PIF to artificially separate B2B SaaS revenue from the operating company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 51 of 2012 and Law 70 of 2019, a determination of artificiality leads to compulsory dissolution of the PIF by the Public Registry, annual franchise tax penalties, fines of up to USD 10,000 for failure to maintain foundation books, and ESR non-compliance penalties up to USD 1,000,000 with cancellation of the tax-residence certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Panamanian courts may pierce the PIF veil on proof of fraudulent conveyance or liability-shielding; founders, beneficial owners, and directors are subject to civil restitution of unpaid taxes and third-party debts, travel bans and attachment orders over personal assets, and criminal imprisonment of two (2) to four (4) years for asset concealment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file and maintain the Registered Agent's Client Due Diligence File under Law 47 of 2013 and Law 23 of 2015; omitting the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner of the SaaS commercial structure; accepting subscription fee settlements from unrelated third parties without KYC evidence; operating the PIF as an opaque conduit for cross-border payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Panamanian Financial Intelligence Unit (UAF) and the banking supervisor can impose fines of USD 1,500 to USD 25,000 per missing record, suspend the registered agent, freeze PIF bank accounts, and confiscate assets; aggravated money-laundering cases trigger criminal fines up to USD 1,000,000 and forfeiture under Article 254 of the Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the PIF compliance officer are personally accountable; travel bans and imprisonment of two (2) to five (5) years may be imposed for active money laundering under Law 23/2015; voluntary remediation before detection reduces exposure to civil fines but does not eliminate the personal criminal liability of natural-person signatories.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and file the mandatory Local File and Transfer Pricing Informative Declaration when B2B SaaS intercompany transactions exceed the USD 3,000,000 threshold; charging software IP licensing fees to the Panamanian PIF at a mark-up outside the arm's length range; neglecting to update the TP documentation for five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A TP corrective adjustment of the taxable base is imposed, plus a penalty of 10% of the adjusted amount (minimum USD 500) when documentation is absent; omission of the informative declaration triggers fines of USD 1,000 to USD 10,000 and monthly 1% interest; the foreign-source exemption claim is disallowed if the transfer price is not at arm's length.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the return are jointly liable for the full TP adjustment, penalties, and interest if they knew of artificial pricing; administrative disqualification and notification to the Public Registry may follow; grossly negligent TP reporting is recharacterized as willful tax evasion and prosecuted against the natural-person directors.
